presentingComplaint: High-grade fever with chills and rigors for 5 days
history: Previously well 32-year-old man, resident of a malaria-endemic district in eastern India, presents with 5 days of intermittent high-grade fever reaching 40 C, preceded by shaking chills and rigors and followed by drenching sweats. Fever has become near-daily with some paroxysms roughly every 48 hours. Associated headache, generalized myalgia, anorexia and two episodes of non-bloody vomiting. No cough, dysuria or diarrhea. Reports several previous episodes of 'malaria' treated locally. No recent antimalarial chemoprophylaxis. No comorbidities, no immunosuppression.
examination: Ill-appearing, febrile and diaphoretic. Mild pallor and scleral subicterus. Spleen palpable 3 cm below costal margin; liver just palpable. No neck stiffness, no focal neurological deficit (GCS 15). Chest clear, no crepitations. No rash, no eschar, no lymphadenopathy. No bleeding manifestations.
imaging: USG abdomen: mild hepatosplenomegaly, no focal lesion, no biliary dilatation
microbiology: Peripheral smear (thick and thin): asexual ring forms and gametocytes of P. falciparum PLUS trophozoites and schizonts with enlarged Schuffner-dotted erythrocytes of P. vivax — mixed infection confirmed. Parasitemia ~1.5% (P. falciparum). Rapid diagnostic test positive for HRP-2 (Pf) and pan-Plasmodium pLDH (non-falciparum). Blood cultures pending.
differentialDiagnoses: Mixed P. falciparum + P. vivax malaria
citations: WHO Guidelines for the Treatment of Malaria 2015
NVBDCP/ICMR National Guidelines for Diagnosis and Treatment of Malaria in India 2014
stewardship: Treat as falciparum given the mixed infection: artemisinin-based combination therapy (artesunate-based ACT, e.g. artemether-lumefantrine or artesunate-sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine per regional policy) for the erythrocytic stage; ADD primaquine 0.25 mg/kg/day for 14 days after G6PD testing to eradicate P. vivax hypnozoites and prevent relapse, plus single-dose gametocytocidal primaquine for falciparum transmission blocking. IV artesunate reserved for severe disease.
contraindications: Primaquine contraindicated in G6PD deficiency (hemolysis) and in pregnancy — test G6PD before radical cure
Avoid halofantrine/QT-prolonging combinations; caution with mefloquine if neuropsychiatric history
edgeCases: Mixed infections frequently under-recognized: P. vivax can be masked by P. falciparum on smear, and treating only falciparum leaves hypnozoites causing later relapse
Watch for progression to severe/cerebral malaria (cerebral impairment, AKI, ARDS, hypoglycemia, DIC) driven by the falciparum component
expectedMaiK: Smear-confirmed mixed P. falciparum + P. vivax infection should be managed as falciparum with an ACT for the acute erythrocytic stage, plus G6PD-guided 14-day primaquine radical cure to clear vivax hypnozoites and prevent relapse. Monitor closely for severe-malaria features from the falciparum component.
expectedNextQuestions: Travel/residence in a malaria-endemic area and prior malaria episodes?
G6PD status and pregnancy status before giving primaquine?
Any features of severe malaria (impaired consciousness, reduced urine output, bleeding, breathlessness)?
expectedInvestigations: Repeat/quantified peripheral smear with parasite count
Renal/liver profile, glucose and lactate to screen for severe malaria

investigations: Peripheral blood smear (thick and thin) with parasite count

crossAccept.rationale: Mixed malaria is a subtype of malaria; same antimalarial pathway.

regressionAssertions: stewardship must include primaquine for vivax radical cure
